9	/-!
10	# The ε-identity does not consume a certificate: it consumes the WINDOW QUOTIENT
11	
12	`Picard/DivRepChartClassUnivAny.lean` weakened U2's residue from "the `Classical.choose`n
13	adaptation is certified" to "*some* adaptation is certified"
14	(`ThetaGeneratorSeed.HasCertifiedAdaptation`).  A fresh-context review then observed that the
15	weakened form is **refuted** by `forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling`
16	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean`) whenever the seed's local equations are connected and
17	meet both pinned vertical fibres — that theorem concludes `∀ A n, ¬ A.IsCertified n`, so it
18	refutes an existential over adaptations exactly as it refutes a property of one adaptation.
19	The `…divrep.u2` row was left **unpriced**.
20	
21	**This file re-prices it, and the answer is that the refutation misses the target.**  Unfold
22	what the ε-identity actually consumes:
23	
24	* `divFamEps` is two `divisorWindow`s (`Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean`), and
25	  `divisorWindow d` reads **only** `d` — no cover, no adaptation, no chart typing;
26	* `divisorWindow_eq_of_le` (`Picard/DivSchemeEps.lean`) is the rank engine
27	  `Submodule.eq_of_le_of_rankAtStalk_quotient_eq` applied to the pair
28	  `x.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow d`.  That engine's hypotheses are three module-theoretic
29	  facts about the **window quotient** `(R ⊗[k] H_a) ⧸ K_a(d)`.
30	
31	The adaptation appears in the landed statement only as a *vehicle* for those three facts:
32	`windowQuotEquiv` transports them from `A.ThetaGlued a`, and `IsCertified` is what makes
33	`A.ThetaGlued a` finite projective of rank `g`.  Cut the vehicle out and the hypothesis is
34	
35	> `(R ⊗[k] H_a) ⧸ K_a(d)` is projective over `R` of constant fibre rank `g`.
36	
37	**Finiteness is not among the inputs, and that is measured rather than assumed.**  The rank
38	engine takes its `Module.Finite` slot at the *Grassmannian point's* quotient, which
39	`grFunctorAff` carries as a field; so the window side owes only projectivity and the rank
40	equation.  The landed chart-typed statement threads finiteness of `A.ThetaGlued a` as well —
41	that hypothesis is genuinely unused on the window side, and dropping it is what the
42	`unusedVariables` linter reported when this file first elaborated.
43	
44	**Why this matters, and it is the point of the file.**  That statement mentions no
45	adaptation, so `forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling` does not bear on it: the no-go's proof
46	runs through clause **(c1)** of `IsCertified` (finiteness of the *chart-local colength*
47	modules forces `supportLeak = ∅`, hence confinement to one pinned chart —
48	`supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified`).  A statement about the window quotient of `d`
49	is not an instance of the refuted `∀`.  So the ε-half of U2 is **open, not false**, and the
50	no-go's bite is confined to the *class* half.
51	
52	## The honest partition this file establishes
53	
54	U2 asks a producer for two things at the universal point, and only one of them is what the
55	no-go refutes:
56	
57	| half | what it needs | vs. the no-go |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| the **ε-value** | `d`'s window quotient is projective of rank `g` | untouched: no adaptation |
60	| the **class** | a term of `DivFamZar C R_Z π g` (locally certified) | the refuted half |
61	
62	So the `…divrep.u2` row should be read as: the ε-layer is carrier-free and no-go-immune, and
63	the whole remaining bite of `I-0705` is on producing the class — which is precisely the half
64	protection `I-0492`'s widening (R2) exists to supply.  That is a strictly sharper statement
65	than "unpriced", and it is what tells the certificate lane which face to widen.
66	
67	## Main declarations
68	
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_quotientData` — the ε-projection identity's
70	  window form from the window quotient alone: no `DivisorAdaptation`, no `IsCertified`.
71	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified_of_quotientData` — the landed
72	  chart-typed statement recovered as a corollary, so the generalisation is machine-checked
73	  rather than asserted.
74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamEps_eq_of_le_of_quotientData` — the ε-**pair** identity for an
75	  arbitrary `F : DivFam C R π g`, from window-quotient data at the two pinned windows.  This
76	  is the form a widened producer can feed, and it never mentions a carrier.
77	
78	## What this does NOT do
79	
80	It produces no certificate, no adaptation and no class, so **no gate clears**: nothing here
81	lets a consumer instantiate `DivRepAffinePullback`.  It re-partitions the debt and removes a
82	*refutation* from one half of it.  Critical-path §7.6 (L8) is untouched.
83	
84	**The honest limit of the headline, and it is the probe this file does not run.**  "The ε-half is
85	open, not false" is a claim about the **no-go**: `forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling` does not
86	bear on a hypothesis that names no adaptation.  It is *silent about satisfiability*.  The mirror
87	risk is real and unmeasured: if the window quotient at the universal point can never be
88	projective of constant rank `g`, then this file has reduced U2's ε-half to a **false**
89	hypothesis — and such a reduction passes every `sorry` census and every axiom probe, because it
90	is then a theorem.
91	
92	Note the asymmetry with the junk-witness probe that refuted DAT-J's Abel square
93	(`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSquareVacuity.lean`): *that* residue was vacuous because its witness was
94	**consumer-chosen**.  Here the window quotient is determined by `d`, so vacuity is impossible and
95	satisfiability is the only live failure mode.  A reduction owes both checks; this one carries
96	"not silently stronger" (the corollary above, which recovers the landed statement) and owes the
97	satisfiability one.
98	-/

134	
135	A Grassmannian point `x` contained in the window submodule `K_a(d)` *equals* it as soon as
136	the window quotient `(R ⊗[k] H_a) ⧸ K_a(d)` is projective over `R` of constant fibre rank

140	This is `divisorWindow_eq_of_le` (`Picard/DivSchemeEps.lean`) with its vehicle removed.  That
141	statement threads an adaptation `A` and asks for finiteness/projectivity/rank of
142	`A.ThetaGlued a`; `windowQuotEquiv` then transports those to the quotient, which is the only
143	place they are used.  Stating them at the quotient is therefore a strict weakening, and it is
144	the weakening that matters: the standing refutation
145	`forall_not_isCertified_of_straddling` quantifies over `DivisorAdaptation`s, and this

147	theorem divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_quotientData
148	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
149	    (x : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
150	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
151	    (hproj : Module.Projective R
152	      ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
153	        divisorWindow d hH1))
154	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
155	      Module.rankAtStalk
156	        ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
157	          divisorWindow d hH1) p = g)
158	    (hle : x.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow d hH1) :
159	    divisorWindow d hH1 = x.toSubmodule := by
160	  haveI := hproj
161	  refine (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_rankAtStalk_quotient_eq hle fun p => ?_).symm
162	  rw [x.rankAtStalk_eq p, hrank p]

164	/-- **The landed chart-typed statement is a corollary** — recorded as a lemma so that the
165	generalisation above is machine-checked rather than asserted in prose.  The three
166	window-quotient facts come from the certificate through `windowQuotEquiv`, exactly as in the
167	landed proof; what the corollary shows is that nothing else in that proof used `A`. -/
168	theorem divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified_of_quotientData
169	    (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d) (hc : A.IsCertified g)
170	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
171	    (x : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k
172	      (↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) g R)
173	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (A.thetaGluedEval a))
174	    (hle : x.toSubmodule ≤ divisorWindow d hH1) :
175	    divisorWindow d hH1 = x.toSubmodule := by
176	  -- the two window-quotient facts, transported off the certificate by `windowQuotEquiv`.
177	  -- The `Module.Finite`/`Module.Projective` slots of `A.ThetaGlued a` are certificate
178	  -- CONSEQUENCES rather than instances, so they are introduced explicitly (`haveI`) before
179	  -- the transport: `Module.Projective.of_equiv` needs the source side in scope, and leaving
180	  -- it to synthesis fails.
181	  haveI := hc.finite_thetaGlued (A := A) a
182	  haveI := hc.projective_thetaGlued (A := A) a
183	  refine divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_quotientData hH1 x
184	    (Module.Projective.of_equiv (windowQuotEquiv A hH1 hsurj).symm) (fun p => ?_) hle
185	  rw [congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv (windowQuotEquiv A hH1 hsurj)) p]
186	  exact hc.rankAtStalk_thetaGlued a p

200	    (x : Grassmannian.grFunctorAff k

202	    (hproj : Module.Projective R
203	      ((R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸ F.window hH1))

208	    (hle : x.toSubmodule ≤ F.window hH1) :
209	    F.window hH1 = x.toSubmodule := by
210	  haveI := hproj
211	  refine (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_rankAtStalk_quotient_eq hle fun p => ?_).symm
212	  rw [x.rankAtStalk_eq p, hrank p]

292	**unsatisfiability** — a reduction to a false hypothesis passes every `sorry` census and axiom

296	unconditionally, on `DivFam`.**  `Picard/DivSchemeFrameCover.lean` carries
297	`DivFam.projective_window_quotient` and `DivFam.rankAtStalk_window_quotient` for *every*

304	* `hle₁` is DDR-3's `le_vanishingSubmodule` at the seed;

8	/-!
9	# U2 does not ask about the CHOSEN adaptation: any certified one will do
10	
11	Every statement of U2's residue so far has been phrased at
12	`ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation` (`Picard/DivSchemeFamily.lean`), which is a
13	`Classical.choose` — `(exists_divisorAdaptation …).some`.  So the recorded obligation reads
14	
15	> `IsCertified g` **for the adaptation the extraction happened to pick**
16	
17	and a producer that builds its own adaptation cannot discharge it, however good that
18	adaptation is.  **That is an artefact of the spelling, not of the mathematics**, and the
19	two landed facts that say so are one line each:
20	
21	* `divisorWindow` "depends only on `d`, not on any chart adaptation" — its own docstring
22	  (`Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean`), and `divFamEps` is two `divisorWindow`s;
23	* `divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified` (`Picard/DivSchemeEps.lean`) takes an
24	  **arbitrary** `A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d` and concludes about `d` alone;
25	* `CertifiedDivisorFamily` (`Picard/DivisorFamily.lean`) is a *triple* `(eqns, adaptation,
26	  certified)` whose `adaptation` field is any adaptation of `eqns` — it never mentions the
27	  extraction.
28	
29	So the honest residue is the existential below, and this file states it and re-derives the
30	whole U2 package from it.  The gain is not a shorter proof; it is that a producer may now
31	**supply its own adaptation**, which is what any certificate-assembly route does (it builds
32	a cover, adapts to it, and certifies *that*).
33	
34	## Main declarations
35	
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.HasCertifiedAdaptation` — the residue: *some*
37	  adaptation of the seed's local-equation system carries a degree-`n` certificate.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.certifiedFamilyOfAdaptation` and
39	  `divFamEps_certifiedFamilyOfAdaptation` — the ε-projection identity from a certificate at
40	  an arbitrary adaptation, the general (seed-level, no chart) form.
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PointwiseAchiever` ·
42	  `exists_divFamZar_divFamEps_eq_universal_pair_of_hasCertifiedAdaptation`
43	  — U2's ε-identity **and** the `DivFamZar` class over the chart ring, from
44	  `HasCertifiedAdaptation` plus `g ≠ 0`, i.e. from the weakest form of the certificate
45	  obligation with no scalar side condition.
46	
47	## What this does NOT do
48	
49	It produces no certificate and no adaptation, so no gate clears.  What changes is the shape
50	of the debt: an existential over adaptations rather than a property of a `Classical.choose`.
51	Critical-path §7.6 (L8) is untouched.
52	
53	**One thing it deliberately does not claim.**  It does not bridge
54	`AffAdaptation.IsCertified` (the widened R2 carrier, `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffAdaptation.lean`)
55	to `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`.  `DivisorAdaptation` extends `FinCoverData`, so a
56	widened cover has no chart typing to recover and manufacturing one is what protection
57	`I-0492` clause 3 forbids.  This file makes the *chart-typed* obligation as weak as it can
58	be; re-typing the ε layer onto the widened adaptation remains the open seam.
59	-/

113	/-- **The split witness predicate** (CHART-U(a) in the `w4-datb` §1.6 (a-amendment)
114	spelling), at a plus class `μ` over a field `K`.
115	
116	A plus class over a field need not be an honest Čech class — it is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for
117	an étale cover `E` of `K`.  The amendment's "for some finite separable `L/κ(t)` splitting
118	the collapsed plus class" is this: there is a finite separable extension `L/K` over which
119	`μ` becomes `relPicMk` of an honest Čech class `M` on `C_L`, and `M` admits an effective
120	witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`.
121	
122	Stated with the witness clause on a *presenting Čech class* rather than on a datum,
123	because the datum layer is where the shifted-datum constructor (DAT-C GAP-1) is missing;
124	the two agree through `Pic0ChartLocusClass.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.
125	
126	## A convention this predicate INHERITS, and which a consumer must not misread
127	
128	The worksheets say "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`".  The witness clause here —
129	and the tree's `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`
130	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`) that it mirrors, and the GAP-6 dictionary
131	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (`DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:182`) that both rest
132	on — asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  It asks only for a `CurveDivisor` in the
133	class with vanishing `H¹`.  That is deliberate on the tree's side: the dictionary is an *iff*
134	against the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗ L)`, and that
135	condition cannot see effectivity or degree, so adding either clause would break the iff and
136	with it the openness route.
137	
138	Two consequences, both load-bearing:
139	
140	* the degree is supplied **externally**, by the chart-index constraint through
141	  `degAt_chartTwist` below: on a degree-zero `λ` the twisted class has fibre degree

143	  hypothesis of this predicate.  (Until 2026-07-28 this read `−g`, and that sign made the

145	  `chartTwist_chartValue` now pins the direction by the kernel);
146	* effectivity likewise is not asserted here.  Where the *worksheet's* stronger reading is

151	def IsSplitWitness {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
152	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) : Prop :=
153	  ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
154	      (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
155	      (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic),
156	    PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
157	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
158	      ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
159	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
160	            ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
161	                ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)

163	/-! ## The twisted fibre family -/
164	
165	variable (C) in
166	/-- **The twisted family whose chart-membership `chartLocus` tests**: the plus class `λ`
167	shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family.
168	
169	This is the *class-side* half of `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`): where
170	`chartValue` twists the Abel class of a divisor family, `chartTwist` twists an arbitrary
171	plus class by the same two factors.  A point of `chartLocus` is precisely a point at which
172	`chartTwist` is realised by an effective divisor with no `H¹` — i.e. at which `λ` itself is
173	a chart value, after undoing the twist. -/
174	def chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : picEt C T :=
176	  lam * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m) * (sigmaFamily C Z T)⁻¹
177	
178	/-- **The degree ledger of the twist**: at every field point the twisted family has fibre
179	degree `m·d₁ − deg Z` when `λ` is degree-zero.  With the chart-index constraint
180	`deg Z = m·d₁ − g` this is `+g`, which is the degree at which an effective witness with
181	`h¹ = 0` can exist at all.
182	
183	**Sign discipline, and it was wrong here until 2026-07-28 (issue I-0514).**  `chartTwist`
184	must be the INVERSE of `chartValue`'s twist, not the same one.  `chartValue` is
185	`abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`), so recovering the Abel class from a chart
186	value means multiplying by `θᵐ` and dividing by `Σ` — hence `chartTwist` is
187	`λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`.  An earlier version applied the `chartValue` twist itself, giving fibre degree
188	`deg Z − m·d₁ = −g`; since `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))` forces `deg W ≥ g − 1`, that locus was
189	**empty for every `g ≥ 1`** and its openness was the openness of `∅`.  The comparison point is
190	`degAt_chartValue` at `n = g` (where the chart index is calibrated and `chartValue` lands in
191	`pic0`), NOT at `n = 0`.
192	
193	**An independent confirmation that `+g` is the right target**, worth recording because the
194	wrong sign survived two sessions: at `deg W = g` the rank anchor
195	`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives, for a
196	witness with `h¹ = 0`,
197	`h⁰ = deg W + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1` — exactly the `h⁰ = 1` normalization that DAT-C §2 and
198	GAP-2's uniqueness both require.  So `+g` is not merely the sign that makes the locus nonempty;
199	it is the unique degree at which the witness is *unique*, which is what the chart map needs to be
200	injective.  At `−g` the same anchor gives `h⁰ = 1 − 2g`, negative for `g ≥ 1` — the contradiction
201	that made the locus empty. -/
202	theorem degAt_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
203	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T)
204	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
205	    degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
206	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
207	  rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
208	    degAt_sigmaFamily, (mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hlam) K t]
209	  ring

211	/-- **`chartTwist` inverts `chartValue`'s twist** — the sign check, as a theorem rather than a
212	docstring claim.
213	
214	Applying `chartTwist` to a chart value returns the Abel class it came from.  This is the
215	statement that was FALSE of the earlier definition (which returned
216	`abelDiv · Σ² · (θᵐ)⁻²`), and it is why the direction is now pinned by the kernel: any future
217	edit to `chartTwist` that breaks the inversion breaks this lemma.
218	
219	Recorded per issue I-0514.  A degree ledger alone does not catch a sign error — the wrong-signed
220	ledger was internally consistent — but an inversion law does. -/
221	theorem chartTwist_chartValue {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ)
222	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
223	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
224	    chartTwist C m Z T (chartValue C π n m Z T s) = abelDiv C π n T s := by
225	  rw [chartTwist, chartValue]
226	  group

232	points of a general test `T` at which the twisted fibre class `λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)` has, after

234	divisor with vanishing `H¹`.

236	The three layers, each supplied by a named brick:
237	* the *point-to-field-point* passage is `Over.testPoint` (input 0 of this brick — the one
238	  nothing in the tree had);
239	* the *twist* is `chartTwist`, the class-side avatar of `chartValue`;
240	* the *split witness reading over a field* is `IsSplitWitness`.

244	def chartLocus (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
245	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) : Set T.left :=
246	  {t : T.left | IsSplitWitness C
247	    (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam))}

250	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left) :
251	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam ↔ IsSplitWitness C
252	      (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)) :=
253	  Iff.rfl

255	/-! ## The datum-layer reading
256	
257	The witness clause of `IsSplitWitness` is stated on a presenting Čech class over `C_L`.
258	The tree's *engine-facing* predicate is stated on a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum`
259	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`), and
260	the two are joined by `exists_cechPicClass_eq` (every class is presented) plus
261	class-intrinsicity.  This is the seam CHART-U(b) crosses to reach
262	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, so it is recorded here as a lemma of the definition
263	rather than left implicit in the openness proof. -/
264	
265	/-- **The witness clause at a splitting field, in datum form**: for a Čech class `M` over
266	`C_L`, admitting an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹` is exactly
267	`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` of any datum presenting `M` — as a class over the base `L` itself,
268	where `relCurveMap C L L` is the identity comparison.
269	
270	Note the datum lives over the *field* `L` as base ring, which is the affine base the
271	engine's `PrimeSpectrum L` has a unique point of; that is why the fibre reading and the
272	base reading coincide here. -/
273	theorem exists_witness_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_datum
274	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
275	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C L π) {M : (relCurve C L).CechPic}
276	    (hD : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass
277	      = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M) :
278	    (∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
279	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M
280	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
281	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1))
282	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := by
283	  rw [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing, hD]
284	
285	/-- **Upward closure of the witness clause along a separable extension of the splitting
286	field** — the substantive half of the (a-amendment)'s "some (equivalently every)".
287	
288	If a Čech class `M` over `C_L` has an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`, then
289	so does its base change to any finite separable `L'/L`.  This is what makes two splittings
290	of the same plus class comparable: pass to a common separable extension and compare there,
291	rather than comparing the two splittings directly.
292	
293	Proof: present `M` by a datum `D` over `L` (`exists_cechPicClass_eq`); the witness clause at
294	`L` is `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L`, which transfers to `L'` by the co-owned separable
295	invariance `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable`
296	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:157` — itself resting only on faithful flatness of a field
297	extension, so separability is packaging, not content). -/
298	theorem exists_witness_of_separable_extension (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
299	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
300	    {L' : Type u} [Field L'] [Algebra k L'] [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower k L L']
301	    [Algebra.IsSeparable L L'] (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
302	    (h : ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
303	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
304	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
305	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
306	    ∃ W' : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left).CurveDivisor,
307	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L' W' = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L') M
308	        ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
309	            ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left.divisorSheaf L' W') 1) := by
310	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (B := L) (π := π) M
311	  obtain ⟨W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
312	  -- the witness clause at `L` is the datum predicate at `L`: `relCurveMap C L L` acts as
313	  -- the identity comparison on classes, since it is `Spec` of the identity algebra map.
314	  have hid : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass := by
315	    have : relCurveMap C L L = 𝟙 (relCurve C L) := by
316	      rw [relCurveMap]
317	      have hom : overSpecMap (k := k) L L = 𝟙 (overSpec k L) :=
318	        Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simp)
319	      rw [hom, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id]
320	      rfl
321	    rw [this, Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
322	    rfl
323	  have hL : D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := ⟨W, by rw [hid, hD, hW], hW1⟩
324	  -- transfer along the separable extension, then read it back as a witness clause
325	  obtain ⟨W', hW', hW1'⟩ :=
326	    (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable L L').mp hL
327	  exact ⟨W', by rw [hW', hD], hW1'⟩

329	/-! ## Naturality — the half CHART-U(b) transport (i) consumes -/
330	
331	/-- **`chartLocus` is compatible with restriction of the class**: the twist commutes with
332	`picEtMap`, so restricting `λ` along a morphism of tests restricts the twisted family too.
333	
334	This is `sigmaFamily_natural` + `thetaFamily_natural` and nothing else; it is stated
335	separately because transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6 (the descent-preimage step) is exactly
336	this identity read at the field point of a point over the source. -/
337	theorem picEtMap_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
338	    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) :
339	    picEtMap C f (chartTwist C m Z T lam)
340	      = chartTwist C m Z T' (picEtMap C f lam) := by
341	  rw [chartTwist, chartTwist, map_mul, map_inv, map_mul, map_pow,
342	    sigmaFamily_natural, thetaFamily_natural]
343	
344	/-- **`chartLocus` pulls back into `chartLocus`** — transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6, in the
345	form the assembly consumes.
346	
347	For `f : T' ⟶ T` and `t : T'.left`, membership of `t` in the pulled-back locus and of `f t`
348	in the original are the *same* condition on the *same* twisted class, read at two fields:
349	`κ(t)` and `κ(f t)`, with `κ(f t) → κ(t)` the induced extension (`testPointFieldMap`).  So
350	the transport is exactly the invariance of `IsSplitWitness` under that extension.
351	
352	**This lemma proves nothing on its own — it is an interface, and its proof is `hinv`.**  Said
353	plainly so that no lane cites it as if transport (i) were discharged.  What it *does* is fix
354	the exact shape of the obligation and put the burden where it belongs: on the morphism `f`,
355	via the field extension `κ(f t) → κ(t)` it induces, rather than hidden inside the locus.  The
356	tree's landed invariance (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable`) discharges `hinv` when
357	that extension is separable — which is the étale-carrier case the (b-amendment) needs, and is
358	*not* automatic for an arbitrary morphism of tests.  The residue between the two is why
359	`hinv` is a hypothesis and not a `rw`. -/
360	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_mem_chartLocus_comp (m : ℕ)
361	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
362	    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t : T'.left)
363	    (hinv : IsSplitWitness C
364	        (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)) (chartTwist C m Z T lam))
365	      → IsSplitWitness C
366	        (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T' (picEtMap C f lam)))) :
367	    f.left.base t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam
368	      → t ∈ chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C f lam) :=
369	  hinv

15	# U2's ε-identity at the universal point, from the certificate alone
16	
17	The DDR9-U ε-identity (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.1 U2) asks that the
18	tautological pair-chart data at the universal point satisfy the ε-identity: over the
19	`Z(♦)`-chart ring `R_Z`, the certified family of the universal seed has
20	
21	> `ε = (x₁, x₂)`  with  `x₁ = divUniversalFstWindow`, `x₂ = divUniversalSndWindow`
22	
23	the universal tautological pair.  This file discharges that identity from **one**
24	hypothesis, `IsCertified`, having found that the other three inputs of the landed
25	ε-projection identity are already available at the universal point.
26	
27	## What was already landed, and had not been composed
28	
29	`ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamEps_certifiedFamily` (`Picard/DivSchemeEps.lean`) takes four
30	inputs beyond the seed: a generator clause `hD`, a certificate `hc`, two `thetaGluedEval`
31	surjectivities, and the second-window containment `hle₂`.  At the universal point:
32	
33	* **`hD` is free** — `PointwiseAchiever.isGenerator_highWindowPointwiseGeneratorSeed`
34	  (`Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowPointwiseGenerator.lean`) is a generator clause for the
35	  seed at `K = divUniversalSeedK`, over `R_Z` itself, from `hO`, `hχ` and
36	  `hb : 0 < windowBound π hπ` only.  It routes through `pointwiseSeedRDN_of_highWindow`,
37	  so it needs **no** germ-divisibility input: it is *not* `isGenerator_seedUniv'`, which
38	  is the seed whose RD-N hypothesis is the recorded geometric wall (I-0302 §residual
39	  2b/2c).  Two different seeds over the same ring, and only one of them is gated.
40	* **`hle₂` is free** — `PointwiseAchiever.divUniversalSndWindow_le_highWindow_divisorWindow`
41	  (`Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowSecondContainment.lean`) is exactly the second-window
42	  containment *for this seed*, from the same three hypotheses.
43	* **both surjectivities are free given `hc`** —
44	  `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified.thetaGluedEval_surjective`
45	  (`Picard/DivisorThetaFibreData.lean`) derives them from the certificate itself, at any
46	  window `≥ M` with the ledger `H¹` input.  The second window is `M + s ≥ M`.
47	
48	So the ε-identity at the universal point is a **corollary of the certificate**, and the
49	composition is what this file records.  Nothing here is new mathematics; what is new is
50	that the four inputs are the *same* seed's, which is why the composite had not been

9	/-!
10	# A DD-R CONSUMER ON THE WIDENED FUNCTOR (R2): `pullGlobal` read at `divFunctorAff`
11	
12	The widened carrier of protection I-0492 acquired a base-change face (ADDENDUM 8), a Zariski
13	gluing keystone (§8.6), and finally a functor `divFunctorAff` with a natural transformation
14	`divFunctorToAff` out of the chart-typed one (ADDENDUM 9).  What it did **not** have, at every
15	one of those milestones, is a **consumer**: measured at HEAD, the widened names appeared in zero
16	files outside the `Picard/DivisorFamilyAff*.lean` family.
17	
18	That is the gap this file closes.  It restates the DD-R general-test pullback
19	(`DivRepAffinePullback.pullGlobal`, `Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean`) on the widened functor and
20	proves the `pull_comp` law there — the one field of `DivRepGlobalData` that is *about* the
21	functor rather than about a single test.
22	
23	## What the restatement costs, and why that is the point
24	
25	Nothing but a push-forward.  `pullGlobalAff` is `divFamZarToAffVehicle ∘ pullGlobal`, and its
26	naturality is the chart-typed `pullGlobal_comp` transported along `divFamZarToAffVehicle_map`.
27	No gluing is redone and no certificate is re-derived over a widened cover.
28	
29	That cheapness is the substantive claim: it says the widened layer is *usable* by the existing
30	DD-R stack, not merely well-formed.  A functor nothing consumes and a functor everything can
31	consume look identical to a sorry census and to a job count.
32	
33	## Direction, once more
34	
35	Old → new.  A consumer that already produces a chart-typed section gets its widened counterpart
36	for free.  The converse does not exist and cannot: by `informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2 /
37	ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 a straddling divisor at genus `≥ 2` is confined by no fixed pair of `P¹` charts.
38	So this file does **not** claim the widened functor is representable by `DivOver`; it claims the
39	chart-typed representability datum pushes forward to a compatible family of widened values.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.pullGlobalAff` — the widened general-test pullback.
44	* `…pullGlobalAff_val` — its value at an affine open, `toAff` of the chart-typed one.
45	* `…pullGlobalAff_comp` — the `pull_comp` law at `divFamZarAff.map`.
46	* `…divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_pullGlobalAff` — affine consistency, through the widened collapse.
47	-/

# The critical path to `Challenge.lean:99`, stated once, with evidence

*Written 2026-07-26 (run 0048 round 4). Every `file:line` below was opened and read during
this pass; nothing here is quoted from a docstring, a roadmap row, or a worksheet without
being checked against the source. That caveat is not decoration — the two standing rules of
this project are that module docstrings announce theorems the files do not declare (I-0349)
and that roadmap summaries are confident and frequently wrong about the Lean
(the `ajcr-roadmap-claims-untrustworthy` memory). Both bit again this round.*

> **ROUND-5 AMENDMENT (run 0048 round 5).** The table in §1 was already stale when it was
> committed, and §2's "one open experiment" had been answered the same round by this file's own
> sibling deliverable. Read §7 at the bottom FIRST: it carries the corrections and the current
> state of the chain. The rest of the file is left as written, because the reasoning is still the
> reasoning; only the status column and §2's closing question have moved.

The point of this document is to replace "six independent mountains" with a single ordered
chain, so that a session can see at a glance which link it is standing on. The chain is
written **backwards from the target**, because that is the only direction in which the
dependencies are actually forced.

## 0. The target, and what is admissible

```lean
noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
  sorry                                              -- Challenge.lean:96-99
```

`archon-protected.yaml` freezes this signature. No hypothesis may be added, so a conditional
restatement is not a discharge. The sanctioned discharge is `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`,
and `instGrpObj := (jacobianData C).grpObj`, both definitional.

`Challenge.lean` holds 15 `sorry`s. The rest of the tree holds exactly one
(`Picard/Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean:268`) — but see §5: that number is not the reassurance it looks
like.

## 1. The chain, backwards

Each link names the Lean object that has to exist. `LANDED` means a sorry-free declaration that
the configured build kernel-checks. `UNROOTED` means the declaration exists in source but
`lake build AlgebraicJacobian` never sees it (§5). `MISSING` means no declaration.

| # | link | Lean | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` | `Challenge.lean:99` | MISSING (the target) |
| L2 | the producer `jacobianData C : JacobianData C` | — | **MISSING**, no producer anywhere |
| L3 | the receptacle `structure JacobianData` and its consumer API | `Picard/JacobianData.lean:87-144` | LANDED |
| L4 | `rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ ⋙ forget).RepresentableBy J` | `JacobianData.lean:93` | field of L3 |
| L5 | descent of the representation from a separably closed stage to `k` | roadmap `dat-g`, `dat-glue` DAT-G0 | MISSING |
| L6 | `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — the 01JJ seam | `Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161-169` | **LANDED** |
| L7 | its input (a): a chart family `f`, `hf` of relatively representable open immersions | roadmap `dat-c` C9b | MISSING |
| L8 | its input (b): `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective … (Sigma.desc f)` | roadmap `dat-b` B-6 | MISSING |
| L9 | what L7/L8 are built from: `(divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver` | `Picard/DivRepKit.lean:114` `representableBy` | UNROOTED |
| L10 | its input: a term of `DivRepGlobalData` | `Picard/DivRepKit.lean:69` | **MISSING — zero producers** |
| L11 | the affine→general lift `DivRepGlobalData.ofAffine` | `Picard/DivRepGlobalClassify.lean:288` `toGlobalData` (+ `:306` `representableBy`) | **DISCHARGED** — row corrected in place 2026-07-29 (§7.14.1); see §7.7 |
| L12 | the affine package `DivRepAffinePullback` | `Picard/DivRepAffKit.lean:167` | structure LANDED, no producer |
| L13 | its `pull` / `isDivRepClassify_pull` fields | — | MISSING, this is **U2** |
| L14 | U2's gate: a certificate for the universal chart family | roadmap `ddr.certificate` | **BLOCKED** (§2) |

L6 deserves emphasis, because the roadmap has never said it plainly: **the hardest-sounding
step, "glue local representability into a scheme", is already done.** `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
consumes mathlib's 01JJ engine and returns exactly the type of `JacobianData.rep`. Everything
above it in the table is assembly; everything below it is the real work.

The two genuinely new pieces of mathematics on the chain are **L11** (which nobody had noticed
was missing) and **L14** (which is blocked, and may be blocked for good).

## 2. L14: why the certificate is blocked, and what is genuinely still open

The certificate route asks a relative divisor to be *confined to one of two pinned charts* of
`P^1`. It cannot be, in general:

* `FinCoverData` types its pieces INTO the two pinned charts by construction —
  `h0 : Fin m0 → Γ(relCurve, V0)` (`Picard/DivisorFamily.lean:166`), `h1` into `V1` (`:168`),
  `pieces := Sum.elim (basicOpen ∘ h0) (basicOpen ∘ h1)` (`:186`).
* clause (c1)-finiteness *is* leak-freeness, so every piece trace is clopen in the support
  (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98`), and a connected support therefore lands in one piece,
  hence one chart: `supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified`
  (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:131`).
* the obstruction is `DivEq`-invariant (`DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean:110`) and survives base
  shrink (`DivSchemeCertZarTransport.lean`), so it bites the quotient `DivFamZar`, not merely a
  representative.

Consequences that are settled and should not be re-litigated:

* Refining the cover, shrinking the base, choosing a cleverer submodule `L`, re-spelling the
  equations, and relaxing the chart-wise partitions to a joint covering are **all provably
  useless**. The sharp form: no repair that keeps the pieces inside the preimages of a FIXED PAIR
  of points of `P^1` can work.
* **Re-basing on the Zariski-local certificate does not help either.** This was worth checking
  and was checked this round. The ε-identity really does consume `IsCertified` through only three
  Zariski-local projections — `divisorWindow_eq_of_le_of_isCertified`
  (`Picard/DivSchemeEps.lean:196`) calls `divisorWindow_eq_of_le` (`:170`), whose hypotheses are
  just `Module.Finite`, `Module.Projective`, constant `rankAtStalk` of `A.ThetaGlued`, plus
  surjectivity of `thetaGluedEval` — and it *can* be re-proved from `IsLocallyCertified` by a
  squeeze over `Localization.Away`, with no `ThetaGlued` base change. But the no-go is about
  **producing** a certificate, not consuming one, and `IsLocallyCertified` fails for exactly the
  divisors `IsCertified` fails for. `DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:30-31` says so verbatim: `DivFamZar`
  is blind to connected divisors meeting both `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)`, over any base, after any
  Zariski shrink, for any adaptation.

What remains open, and it is the one cheap decisive experiment:

> The no-go's argument is degree-agnostic, but the only witness ever exhibited
> (`F = tX² + XY + tY²` over `k[t]`, `C = P¹`, `pi = id`) has degree 2 on a curve of genus 0,
> and the functor pins the degree to the genus. At `g = 0` the no-go is vacuous; at `g = 1` base
> shrink evades it. **At `g ≥ 2` no witness has ever been exhibited.**

Either a `g ≥ 2` witness exists — and then the certificate route as designed is dead over an
arbitrary field, and the campaign must pick exactly one of R1 (vary the pinned pair; needs
`Aut(P^1)`, roadmap leaf `p1-aut`), R2 (generalise `FinCoverData`'s piece type), or descent from a
large field (roadmap leaf `dat-g`) — or no witness exists, and the certificate route reopens and
several roadmap leaves are deleted. It is not acceptable to keep planning without knowing which.

A further constraint on R1 that is not optional: the pointwise certificate gate needs two
`κ(p)`-rational points of `P^1` off the fibre's support image at every prime `p`. Over a small
finite residue field, `|P^1(κ(p))| = q + 1` can be smaller than the degree plus two. Since
`Challenge.lean` states the Jacobian over an ARBITRARY field, R1 alone cannot suffice; it needs
the descent lane behind it. That is inbox I-0346's question, and it is the same obstruction seen

## 7.6 The gate is L8, not U2 — and that is the round's main finding

Inbox **I-0365**. The framing "the divrep tail is independent of the certificate; the certificate
gates U2" is false, but not in the direction the tree assumed.

`DivFamZar` is **by definition** a quotient of *locally certified* families
(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:224` the setoid, `:235` the def, `:71` `IsLocallyCertified` — note it
localises on the base only). So certificates are **free on the consuming side**:
`DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover` (`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean:433`) is a landed theorem,
unfolded by every classifier keystone (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:128/:176/:230`,
`DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean:361/:363`), and `IsDivRepClassify` (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:90`)
quantifies over certified families as a *hypothesis*, so their scarcity makes it easier, not harder.

The bite is on the other side. The no-go (`DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:123` — clause (c1) *is*
leak-freeness — and `:131`) says `DivFamZar` is blind to connected divisors meeting both pinned
fibres. So `divFunctor C π g` is a **proper subfunctor** of degree-`g` relative divisors.
Representing it is not the problem; the L9–L13 tail does that honestly. The problem is that a
too-small divisor functor **cannot cover Pic⁰**: the Abel map out of it is not Zariski-locally
surjective, because the classes whose only witnesses are the invisible divisors are never hit.

One nuance that sharpens where to look: the no-go's hypothesis is `IsPreconnected d.supportLocus`,
and **over a field it is vacuous** — the support of a divisor is a finite set of closed points, so
preconnected forces a single point, which cannot meet two disjoint fibres. The blindness is a
purely *relative* phenomenon: a family over a positive-dimensional base whose total support is a
connected horizontal curve sweeping from `π⁻¹(0)` to `π⁻¹(∞)` is invisible, and base shrinking does
not help because every neighbourhood of the crossing contains points on both sides. So
Riemann–Roch-level, fibrewise coverage is untouched — but local surjectivity of a *presheaf* map is
tested on arbitrary scheme tests, which is exactly the relative direction.

**Consequences.** (i) Stop calling U2 or the affine package "the gate": they are tail work and are
nearly finished. (ii) Do not attack L8 against `divFunctor` as it stands — it is arguably false,
not merely hard. (iii) Judge R1 and R2 by whether they widen `DivFamZar` enough for L8, not by
whether they make a certificate easier to prove. A third widening is worth costing beside them:
replace `IsLocallyCertified` outright by the standard relative effective Cartier divisor (finite
locally free of rank `g` over the base), which carries no chart-adaptation artifact at all.

variable (C) in
/-- **The residue-field-iso invariance of the split-witness predicate** — the obligation the
general-test assembly actually rests on, named rather than hidden.

`mem_chartLocus_of_mem_chartLocus_comp` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:360`) says transport (i) "proves
nothing on its own — it is an interface, and its proof is `hinv`", and that the tree's landed
invariance discharges `hinv` for *separable* residue-field extensions.  For an affine-open test
object the extension is an **isomorphism** (`Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso` — hence in
particular separable), so morally transport (i) is free here.

**But the landed invariance is about `HasWitnessH1Vanishing`, not about `IsSplitWitness`**, and no
declaration in the tree transports `IsSplitWitness` along a field isomorphism: measured, the only
mentions of `IsSplitWitness` invariance are two docstring sentences.  So the affine-piece case of
transport (i) needs *one* lemma the tree does not have, which is this predicate.  That is a
correction to `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s claim that the general-test statement "needs no new
mathematics": it needs exactly this, and nothing else.

Why it is believable and small: `IsSplitWitness C μ` is an existential over a finite separable
`L/K` presenting `μ`.  Along an isomorphism `K ≃ K'` the same `L` presents the transported class,
because `PicEtAff.map` composes (`PicEtAff.map_map`) and the inverse iso undoes the transport —
i.e. it is `map_map` plus `map_id`, not geometry.  It is stated as a class-free hypothesis here so
that the assembly below is usable the moment a lane proves it. -/
def IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant : Prop :=
  ∀ (T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))) (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left)
    (_ : IsIso (Over.testPointFieldMap f t)) (mu : picEt C T),
      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (picEtMap C f mu))
        ↔ IsSplitWitness C
            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)) mu)

variable (C) in
/-- **The split-witness predicate agrees along an affine-open test object**, given the
iso-invariance.

This is transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6 for the affine-piece maps, in **both** directions — so
the locus over the piece and the locus over `T` correspond exactly, which is what the locality
assembly needs (a one-sided containment would not give openness).

The only input beyond landed material is `hinv`; the `IsIso` it is applied at is discharged by
`Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso`, i.e. structurally, by mathlib's fact that an open
immersion induces an isomorphism of residue fields. -/
theorem isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) (mu : picEt C T)
    (t : (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)).left) :
    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t)
        (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) mu))
      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C
          (Over.testPoint (T := T) ((Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base t)) mu) :=
  hinv T (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) t
    (Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso T U t) mu

/-- **The affine piece's locus is the preimage of the general-test locus.**

For an affine open `U ⊆ T.left`, `chartLocus` over the affine test object `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` is

`isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff` applied pointwise together with `picEtMap_chartTwist` (the
twist commutes with restriction). -/

    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)

### 7.3 §2's "one open experiment" was already answered, by this file's own sibling

§2 closes with *"At `g ≥ 2` no witness has ever been exhibited… It is not acceptable to keep
planning without knowing which."* That question was settled in the **same round**:
`informal/spec-dd-r.md` **ADDENDUM 4** (commit `d7e8348ce`) is titled *"the on-stratum witness
EXISTS"*, and roadmap leaf `…ddr.certificate.field-size` is `done` carrying the sharp theorem.

**The conclusion stands on ADDENDUM 4, not on what follows.** A ground review corrected the
first draft of this subsection, which claimed the argument below "agrees with" ADDENDUM 4 and holds
"over any field". It does neither. ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 uses the universal divisor over `Sym^g C`,
base-changes to an extension and pads by `(g−1)Q₀`, and states at `spec-dd-r.md:826` that no
rational-point hypothesis is used anywhere. What follows is a **different, cheaper witness** — a
pencil rather than `Sym^g` — with a side condition ADDENDUM 4 does not need:

> For any `g ≥ 2`, take a pencil of degree `g` on `C` one of whose members is a divisor
> `E ≥ s₀ + s_∞` with `π(s₀) = 0`, `π(s_∞) = ∞`. Such an `E` exists: `ℓ(E) = 1 + ℓ(K − E)`, so any
> `E` with `s₀ + s_∞ ≤ E ≤ K'` for a canonical `K' ≥ s₀ + s_∞` has `ℓ(E) ≥ 2`; and such a `K'`
> exists because `ℓ(K − s₀ − s_∞) ≥ g − 2 ≥ 1` for `g ≥ 3`, and for `g = 2` exactly when `s_∞` is
> the hyperelliptic conjugate of `s₀` (which one is free to arrange, since `π` is a choice: a
> function with a zero at `s₀` and a pole at `s_∞` is a finite map sending them to `0` and `∞`).
> The support of the total family is an open subscheme of the irreducible `C`, hence irreducible,
> hence **connected after every Zariski shrink of the base** — which is exactly why the shrink
> evasion that kills the `g = 1` case does not apply here.

**The side condition, and it is not cosmetic.** Writing `s₀ + s_∞` and computing
`ℓ(K − s₀ − s_∞) ≥ g − 2` treats `s₀, s_∞` as *degree-1* points. Over a non-closed field the
minimal closed points `q₀ ∈ π⁻¹(0)`, `q₁ ∈ π⁻¹(∞)` have residue degrees `e₀, e₁`, and an effective
`E ≥ q₀ + q₁` of degree `g` exists only if **`e₀ + e₁ ≤ g`**. Over `𝔽₂` with `g = 2` and
`e₀ = e₁ = 2` this witness does not exist — which is exactly the regime ADDENDUM 4 §4.4's
"only if" direction isolates. Secondly, the `g = 2` case above needs `π` chosen so that `s_∞` is
the hyperelliptic conjugate of `s₀`, whereas ADDENDUM 4 holds for any finite dominant `π`.

So: **the fixed-pair certificate route is dead on the campaign's own stratum** — on ADDENDUM 4's
authority, for every field; and the pencil above is a cheaper witness for the sub-case
`e₀ + e₁ ≤ g`. Do not re-run this experiment. Do not formalise either witness — ADDENDUM 4 §4.5
explains why (it needs `Sym^g C` / `Hilb^g`, and this tree constructs no curve other than `P¹`).

### 7.4 The live strategic question is R1 versus R2, and it is not "which is cheaper"

With the fixed pair dead, `spec-dd-r` ADDENDUM 4 §4.4 leaves exactly two repairs, and they differ
in kind, not only in cost:

* **R1** (`p1-aut` → `fibre-avoid` → `cert-relocalize`): let the certificate quantify over a twist
  `γ ∈ Aut(P¹_k)`. Proved correct **iff `|P¹(k)| ≥ g + 2`** — i.e. over every infinite field and
  over `𝔽_q` for `q ≥ g + 1`, and dead over small finite fields. Since `Challenge.lean` states the
  Jacobian over an **arbitrary** field and `archon-protected.yaml` forbids adding a hypothesis, R1
  **cannot discharge the challenge on its own**: it must be paired with the descent lane `dat-g`.
* **R2** (generalise `FinCoverData`'s piece type from basic opens of the two pinned charts to
  arbitrary affine opens of the relative curve): field-uniform, and ADDENDUM 4 §4.4 gives it a
  one-line justification — `supp D` is finite over `R`, hence contained in a single affine open of
  `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks 0B8B), so a cover with one straddling piece always exists. Blast radius
  measured this round: `FinCoverData` is named in **28 files**.

The honest comparison is therefore *R1 + a full Galois-descent campaign* against *R2 + a 28-file
refactor*. Nobody has costed the second half of R1, and the roadmap's `p1-aut` leaf says "do not
attempt both". That decision is the highest-value thing the next session can make, and it should be
made with a costing of `dat-g`, not with a costing of `p1-aut` alone.

### 7.5 What `Challenge.lean:99` reduces to today

Composing with the frozen discharge `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`, the target is now exactly:

> **a Zariski atlas of `pic0SigmaFunctor C`** — an index `ι`, schemes `X i`, maps
> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that (1) each `f i` is a relatively
> representable open immersion, (2) `Sigma.desc f` is Zariski-locally surjective, (3) each chart's
> structure morphism is locally of finite type and the glued object is quasi-compact.

Sheafhood, the 01JJ gluing, the Σ-descent and both finiteness certificates are discharged.

**Three corrections a ground review forced on the first draft of this subsection, all of which
matter to anyone planning off it.**

* **The atlas is NOT finite, so the producer to aim at is `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace`
  (`JacobianDataCharts.lean:199`), not `ofCharts`.** The chart index is
  `ChartIndex C := (m : ℕ) × {Σ // 0 ≤ Σ ∧ deg Σ = m·d₁ − g}` (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md:161`),
  a `Σ` over all `m : ℕ`, and the worksheet says at :66-71 that the `m`-strata do not collapse, so
  no uniform bound exists. `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never needed finiteness (being locally of
  finite type is local on the source); the whole finiteness burden therefore collapses onto the
  single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued object — which is the DAT-J image argument, a
  theorem about the Jacobian and not bookkeeping.
* **Clause (2) is not a free-standing leaf; it IS the gate.** The only builder of an `f i` is
  `abelSigmaChart` (`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:203`), which consumes

  certified* families (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarFunctor.lean:41-45`). So (2) asserts that certified
  families cover — which is exactly what the no-go denies. See §7.6.
* Only clause (3) is genuinely cheap.

degree constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − n`, the chart value of `DivSchemeAbel.lean` — the Abel class

The degree ledger of `degAt_chartValue` is what makes the target the degree-*zero* functor:
the three factors contribute `n`, `deg Z` and `−m·d₁`, which the constraint sums to zero. -/
def chartValueTrans (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z

    chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg T.unop s⟩

    refine ConcreteCategory.hom_ext _ _ fun s => ?_
    exact Subtype.ext ((picEtMap_chartValue C π n m Z g.unop s).symm)

lemma chartValueTrans_app_coe (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z

/-! ## The Abel chart map -/

variable (C π n) in
/-- **The Abel chart map** of a representation of the divisor functor: the morphism of big-site
presheaves `yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` sending a `D`-point to the degree-zero class
of the divisor family that point names.

`rep` is a *hypothesis* — this file never constructs a representation of the divisor functor;
that is the divisor-representability obligation of the `DivRep…` lane.  Given one, this is the
Abel–Jacobi map at the level of the Σ-extension, and it is the only kind of object
`JacobianData.ofCharts` accepts. -/
def abelSigmaChart {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) :
    yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
  rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (chartValueTrans C π n m Z hdeg)

/-- **The structure morphism of the Abel chart is that of the representing object**: for the
one-element family consisting of the Abel chart map, the chart structure morphism `chartHom`
that `JacobianData.ofCharts` reads off is `D.hom` itself.

So the finiteness hypotheses of the producer, specialised to this chart, are exactly
`LocallyOfFiniteType D.hom` and `CompactSpace D.left` — properties of the divisor scheme, with
no reference to the Picard functor. -/
lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChart {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
    {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) i = D.hom :=
  Category.id_comp _

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

106	
107	variable {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
108	  (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
109	
110	/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart** over the base field: the Σ-component of the
111	element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.  A chart of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
112	is by construction a scheme *together with* a map to `Spec k`, namely the base over which the
113	line bundle it classifies lives; this is that map. -/
114	noncomputable def chartHom (i : ι) : X i ⟶ Spec (.of k) := (yonedaEquiv (f i)).1
115	
116	variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
117	variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
118	
119	/-- **The structure morphism of the glued object of a chart family**: mathlib's 01JJ engine
120	glues the charts into a scheme representing the Σ-extension sheaf, and the Σ-component of the
121	universal element of that representation is the map of that scheme to `Spec k`. -/
122	noncomputable abbrev gluedHom :
123	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
124	  ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
125	    (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1
126	
127	/-- **The glued object of a chart family**, as a scheme over the base field.  This is the
128	object represented by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/
129	noncomputable abbrev gluedOfCharts : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (gluedHom C f hf)
130	
131	/-- The universal element of the glued representation restricts along the `i`-th glue map to
132	the element classified by `f i`. -/
133	lemma representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued (i : ι) :
134	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
135	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i) = yonedaEquiv (f i) :=
136	  Scheme.LocalRepresentability.yonedaGluedToSheaf_app_toGlued hf
137	
138	/-- **The charts are charts over the base field**: the `i`-th glue map into the glued object,
139	followed by the structure morphism of the glued object, is the structure morphism of the `i`-th
140	chart.  Both sides are Σ-components of the same restriction of the universal element. -/
141	lemma toGlued_comp_gluedHom (i : ι) :
142	    Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i ≫ gluedHom C f hf = chartHom C f i := by
143	  have h := congrArg Sigma.fst
144	    ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv_eq
145	      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i))
146	  rw [representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued] at h
147	  exact h.symm
148	
149	/-! ## The two finiteness certificates from the charts -/
150	
151	/-- **Locally of finite type descends from the charts**: the property is local on the source
152	and the glue maps of the glue data cover the glued object, so if each chart is locally of finite
153	type over the base field then so is the glued object. -/
154	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)) :
155	    LocallyOfFiniteType (gluedHom C f hf) := by
156	  refine IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover
157	    (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover fun i => ?_
158	  have h := hlft i
159	  rwa [← toGlued_comp_gluedHom C f hf i] at h
160	
161	/-- **Quasi-compactness descends from a finite family of quasi-compact charts**: the base
162	`Spec k` is affine, so quasi-compactness of the structure morphism is compactness of the space
163	of the glued object, and that space is the union of the finitely many compact chart images. -/
164	theorem quasiCompact_gluedHom [Finite ι] (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
165	    QuasiCompact (gluedHom C f hf) := by
166	  haveI : Finite (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.I₀ := ‹Finite ι›
167	  haveI : ∀ i, CompactSpace ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.X i) := hcpt
168	  haveI : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued :=
169	    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace
170	  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
171	
172	/-! ## The producer -/
173	
174	/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively
175	representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,
176	jointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally
177	of finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.
178	
179	The representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the
180	Σ-component of the universal element; the two certificates are `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`
181	and `quasiCompact_gluedHom`. -/
182	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofCharts [Finite ι]
183	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
184	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
185	    JacobianData C :=
186	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
187	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
188	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
189	    (quasiCompact_gluedHom C f hf hcpt)
190	
191	@[simp]
192	lemma JacobianData.ofCharts_J [Finite ι]
193	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
194	    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
195	    (JacobianData.ofCharts C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
196	  rfl
197	
198	/-- **The producer for an infinite atlas**: same as `JacobianData.ofCharts`, but the index type
199	is arbitrary and quasi-compactness of the glued object is supplied directly instead of being
200	derived from finitely many compact charts.
201	
202	This is the form the classical construction needs.  The charts of the degree-zero Picard functor
203	are indexed by divisor *classes* — one chart per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective
204	witness — and that index set is not finite; compactness of the glued object is then a genuine
205	theorem about the Jacobian (it is the union of the images of a *quasi-compact* divisor scheme
206	under the Abel map), not a consequence of finiteness of the atlas.  Note that the
207	locally-of-finite-type certificate still descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis
208	whatsoever: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never uses `Finite ι`. -/
209	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace
210	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
211	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
212	    JacobianData C :=
213	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
214	    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
215	    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
216	    (HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr hcpt)
217	
218	@[simp]
219	lemma JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace_J
220	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
221	    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
222	    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
223	  rfl
224	
225	end Charts
226	
227	/-! ## The hypothesis bundle of the frozen `Jacobian` suffices
228	
229	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean` introduces `[GeometricallyReduced C.hom]` before its sheaf and
230	representability statements, while the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` carries only
231	`IsProper`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIrreducible`.  There is no gap:
232	geometric reducedness is *derived* from smoothness of relative dimension one by the global
233	instances of `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`, which is in the import closure of
234	`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean`.  Hence every declaration above elaborates under the frozen bundle alone,
235	and the example below records it. -/
236	
237	example : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := inferInstance
238	
239	/-! ## What remains
240	
241	`JacobianData.ofCharts` reduces the frozen `Jacobian` of `Challenge.lean` — that is, the
242	production of `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, from which `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` —
243	to a single geometric statement about the degree-zero Picard sheaf of the curve, namely the
244	existence of a finite Zariski atlas:
245	
246	> there exist a finite index type `ι`, schemes `X : ι → Scheme`, and morphisms of presheaves
247	> `f i : yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaFunctor C` such that
248	>
249	> 1. **(relative representability)** each `f i` is a relatively representable open immersion,
250	>    `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`;
251	> 2. **(coverage)** the family is jointly locally surjective for the big Zariski topology,
252	>    `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)`;
253	> 3. **(chart finiteness)** each chart is locally of finite type over the base field with
254	>    respect to its own structure morphism, `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`, and each
255	>    chart space is quasi-compact, `CompactSpace (X i)`.
256	
257	Nothing else about the Picard functor is needed: the sheaf condition is already discharged
258	(`pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf`), the gluing is mathlib's (`Scheme.LocalRepresentability`), the
259	Σ-descent to the slice is already discharged (`Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice`), and the two
260	certificates of the glued object are discharged here from (3).
261	
262	Conditions (1) and (2) are the geometric input — they are what the divisor-scheme/Abel-map
263	machinery of the `DivScheme…` and `DivRep…` files exists to produce, one chart being carved out
264	of a symmetric power of the curve by an effectivity locus.  Condition (3) is a property of those
265	charts alone and does not interact with the Picard functor at all.
266	
267	If the atlas that machinery produces is *not* finitely indexed — and the classical one is not,
268	its charts being indexed by divisor classes — then `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` is the
269	form to use: `ι` is then arbitrary, condition (3) weakens to `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)`
270	alone, and the second certificate becomes the single statement `CompactSpace` of the glued
271	object.  That statement is not a bookkeeping hypothesis but a theorem about the Jacobian — the
272	underlying space is the image of a quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map — and it is
273	where the quasi-compactness content of the construction actually lives. -/
274	
275	end AlgebraicGeometry

theorem windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero (hg : g ≠ 0) : 0 < windowBound pi hpi :=

            (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg)).certifiedFamily g
          (isGenerator_univSeed C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hO hchi
            (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg)) hc))
      = ((divUniversalFstWindow C pi hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j).toSubmodule,

/-- **The existential form with no scalar hypothesis** — what a chart-class producer
consumes once it knows the genus is nonzero. -/

    (hc : ((univSeed C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hO hchi
      (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg)).divisorAdaptation
      (isGenerator_univSeed C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hO hchi
        (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg))).IsCertified g) :
    ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C RZ pi g,

        = ((divUniversalFstWindow C pi hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j).toSubmodule,
           (divUniversalSndWindow C pi hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j).toSubmodule) :=
  ⟨_, divFamEps_highWindow_eq_universal_pair_of_ne_zero
    C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hO hchi hg hc⟩

/-- **The `DivFamZar` class of the universal point with no scalar hypothesis.** -/
noncomputable def divFamZarUnivOfNeZero (hg : g ≠ 0)
    (hc : ((univSeed C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hO hchi
      (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg)).divisorAdaptation
      (isGenerator_univSeed C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hO hchi
        (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg))).IsCertified g) :
    DivFamZar C RZ pi g :=

    (windowBound_pos_of_ne_zero C hpi g hO hchi hg) hc

discharge route `grpObj` (`:113-114`), the whole consumer API

DAT-J does not build it.**  DAT-J's own new mathematics is exactly THREE things (§0.3): the
**producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, its **`quasiCompact` field** via the Abel
image of `Div^g`-lite, and the **definitional discharge** of the two frozen `Challenge.lean`
def-sorries `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj`.  All three are bounded assembly of landed keystones
plus ONE genuinely new but small brick (the qc surjectivity), gated only on the descent

`Picard/JacobianData.lean` consumers and the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` discharge."

whole point of "where the properness boundary sits"):

|---|---|---|---|---|

it stores `locallyOfFiniteType` + `quasiCompact` and NOTHING else.  Separatedness of `d.J`

(`AbelSource.lean:126`, done — *conditional* on the blocked `AbelSourceData` producer P1).

the HEAVY half** (proper source = universal-closedness of the Grassmannian/`Div^g`, the

**Found this pass, HIGH-VALUE, no prior worksheet records it.**  `Jacobian` and
`instGrpObj` are **`def`/`instance` sorries** (`Challenge.lean:96,107`), not `theorem`

## §2 THE qc-VIA-ABEL-IMAGE MECHANISM (the node headline)

### §2.1 Why `d.J` is NOT quasi-compact from the glue

`d.J.left` is 01JJ's `(glueData hf).glued` over the **infinite** `ChartIndex C = (m, Σ)`
(`Type u`; datglue §3.2, datc §3.2).  An infinite open cover glues to a non-compact space in
general — qc is **not** free from the assembly.  It is a posteriori, exactly as the datum
storing `quasiCompact` as a *field* (not deriving it structurally) signals.

### §2.2 The a-posteriori argument (compact `Div^g` + surjective Abel; the field docstring, verbatim)

`JacobianData.lean:97-98` freezes the mechanism: *"a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map."*  Precisely, to prove `QuasiCompact J.hom`
with affine base `Spec (.of k)` it suffices to prove `CompactSpace J.left` (the in-tree
pattern `HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr`, used verbatim at
`DivSchemeQProj.lean:86-88` for `grPair`).  Then:

1. **The source is compact.**  `compactSpace_divScheme` (`DivSchemeQProj.lean:194-195`,
   LANDED, I-0245) — `DivScheme g` is a closed subscheme of the finite-affine-atlas
   Grassmannian pair, hence `CompactSpace`.  (qc of its structure map:
   `quasiCompact_divSchemeOverHom` `:188-190`.)
2. **The Abel map is a morphism `Div^g → J`.**  `abel := d.rep.homEquiv.symm (μ)` where `μ`
   is the universal degree-`g` divisor-family class shifted into `pic0Subgroup` by the
   fiberTwist shifter (§2.3).  Its underlying `abel.left : DivScheme.left → J.left` is
   continuous (`Scheme.Hom.continuous`).
3. **The Abel map is surjective on points** (§2.3).  `Surjective abel.left`.
4. **Image of compact under continuous surjective is compact** — so `CompactSpace J.left`
   (DJ-0, §2.4).  Hence `QuasiCompact J.hom`.

### §2.3 The surjectivity: effectivity + fiberTwist, spelled Challenge-FREE (the honest brick DJ-1)

Every field point of `J.left` is (via a residue-field point through `homEquiv`) a degree-0
class `λ ∈ pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)`.  Shift it by `fiberTwist`:

* `fiberTwist π n` (`FiberTwist.lean:301`), `classDeg_fiberTwist` (`:393`) — degree scales
  linearly, **no `k`-rational point required** (AbelSource docstring `:62`).  Choose `n`
  large so `deg(λ·θ^n) = n·d₁ ≥ g`.
* `exists_effective_of_picClass` (`FLVClass.lean:208`) — a class of degree `≥` the
  genus-free bound has an **effective** representative (its engine is `riemann_inequality`,
  `FLVClass.lean:205/214`, the **genus-FREE** spelling).  The effective representative is a
  point of `Div^g`-lite hitting `λ·θ^n`, hence (un-shifting) `λ` is in the Abel image.
* **Challenge-free (BINDING, §0.5):** use `exists_effective_of_picClass`/`riemann_inequality`
  (FLVClass, Challenge-free cone), **NEVER** `riemann_inequality_curve`
  (`ChiCurve.lean:183`, which imports `Challenge.lean:11`).  This is the SAME surjectivity
  Wave-5's `AbelSourceData.surjective` field uses (`AbelSource.lean:60-69`) — but Wave-5 may
  spell it with `genus` (it is a consumer); DAT-J may not (it is upstream of `Challenge`).
* Base-change of surjectivity to every field is FREE: `MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
  @Surjective` (mathlib `PullbackCarrier.lean:431`, cited `AbelSource.lean:41`).

**DJ-1 is the node's one honest (but small, M-sized) new brick.**  It is *lighter* than
Wave-5's P1: it needs only `compactSpace_divScheme` + surjectivity, never the proper source.

### §2.4 The abstract qc lemma (DJ-0 — launchable NOW, no `rep`)

The reusable core, pure scheme topology, no `divRep`:

> **DJ-0.**  For `f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes with `[CompactSpace X] (hf : Function.Surjective
> f.base)`, `CompactSpace Y`.  (Then, for `g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)` with `Y` affine base:
> `QuasiCompact g` via `HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr`, the `DivSchemeQProj.lean:88`
> pattern.)

Route: `IsCompact.image` / `CompactSpace` of a continuous surjective image (mathlib
`Topology/*`); the in-tree twin for the irreducible analogue is `Function.Surjective.
irreducibleSpace` (`Topology/Irreducible.lean:540`, used `AbelSource.lean:157`) and the qc
analogue `QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace` (used `DivSchemeQProj.lean:82,145`).
**DJ-0 is a `≤ 60`-line mathlib-only brick; write it cold today** as the qc field's engine.

### §2.5 The light-vs-heavy split, restated as the discipline

`quasiCompact` (DAT-J) ← `compactSpace_divScheme` (DD-Q, LANDED) + DJ-1 surjectivity.
`IsProper` (Wave-5) ← `AbelSourceData` whose `isProper` field needs universal-closedness of
`Div^g`/`grPair` — **NOT delivered by DD-Q** (`DivSchemeQProj.lean:44-51`, I-0245 boundary),
a NEW Wave-5 brick, gate `w5-av.p1` **BLOCKED**.  **DAT-J must never import that debt into
its qc field** (§5 risk 3).

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartTwistCollapse

/-!
# A plus class becomes honest over its own étale carrier — over an ARBITRARY affine base

This closes the obligation the CHART-U(b) header table names "honesty over a general affine
base" (issue I-0558), and it needs no field.

## The obligation, and why it looked hard

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean`'s route needs a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over an affine base
whose class is the (collapsed) twisted class.  `exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass`
(`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`) supplies the datum — but it takes an **honest Čech
class** `c` over the base as a *hypothesis*, and a plus class over `Spec A` is not honest: it is
`PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E` of `A`.

The tree's only route from a plus class to an honest one was
`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s `exists_splitting_of_picEt`, which requires `[Field K]` — its
engine is étale field-cofinality (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`),
false over a general base.  So the obligation read as: find a *substitute* for cofinality over
`Spec A`.

## Why it is in fact free

There is no substitute needed, because **a cover splits over its own carrier**.  The
field-cofinality theorem is used to produce an `A`-algebra map `E.Carrier →ₐ L` into something
where the class becomes a unit; but the identity `E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier` is already such a
map, and it exists for every cover over every base.  Restricting the plus class along
`A → E.Carrier` therefore makes it honest, with no finiteness, separability, or field
hypothesis anywhere.

Concretely `PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x` — the
transported class is presented by `x` itself.  The proof is the general-base analogue of
`PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom` (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`), which is stated
only for fields; the field hypotheses there are inherited from *its* consumer (the degree seam,
which reads a degree and so needs a field), not required by the argument.  The one substantive
step is the same in both: the descent condition `x.2`, fed to `relPicAlgMap_congr`, identifies
the two ways of transporting `x` to the base-changed carrier.

## What this does and does not give

It gives honesty **over `Spec E.Carrier`**, not over `Spec A`.  That is exactly what the
(b-amendment) asks for — its step is "over the étale carrier `B := E.Carrier` the class is
honest", after which the engine fires on `Spec B` and transport (ii) pushes the open locus down
to `Spec A` along the (open, surjective) carrier map.  Nothing here performs that descent; the
topological core of it is landed as `isOpen_of_isOpen_comap_preimage`
(`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean:129`).

So after this file the CHART-U(b) route has ONE remaining obligation, the pointwise
`IsChartDatumPresentation` — and, unlike the previous "one remaining obligation" claims on this
lane, that one is a genuine statement about matching two fibre predicates, not a missing
construction.

## Main declarations

`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`

The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)

variable (C π) in
/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.

So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
  huniv i

variable (C π) in
/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**

`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
carries no uniformity obligation.

Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf

end

8	/-!
9	# DJ-1, the topological half: point surjectivity from residue-field lifts
10	
11	`Picard/JacobianDataAbelImage.lean` reduced DAT-J's quasi-compactness field to a single
12	statement, `Function.Surjective abel.base` — *step 3* of `informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md`
13	§2.2, the node's one honest brick.  §2.3 describes the argument for it in the language the
14	Picard theory supplies: *every field point of `J.left` is a degree-zero class over its
15	residue field, shift it by `fiberTwist`, take an effective representative, and that
16	representative is a `DivScheme`-point hitting the original point.*
17	
18	That argument produces, for a point `y`, a **morphism** `Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g` — not an
19	element of the fibre of `abel.base` over `y`.  Nothing in the tree converted the first into
20	the second, and it is not bookkeeping that can be skipped: the target of DJ-1 is a statement
21	about the underlying *topological* map, while everything the Picard side produces is a
22	morphism of schemes.
23	
24	This file supplies exactly that conversion, and nothing else:
25	
26	> `surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` — if for every `y : Y` some
27	> `q : Spec (Y.residueField y) ⟶ X` satisfies `q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y`, then
28	> `f.base` is surjective.
29	
30	The proof is `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField` (mathlib): the range of
31	`Y.fromSpecResidueField y` is `{y}`, and `Spec κ(y)` is nonempty because `κ(y)` is a field,
32	so any point of `Spec κ(y)` maps into the fibre.  Composed with the DJ-0 lemmas this gives
33	the Jacobian datum producers in the shape the classical argument actually delivers: a
34	*per-point lift*, which is what `exists_effective_of_picClass` hands back.
35	
36	## Main declarations
37	
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` — the conversion.
39	  Pure scheme topology; no curve, no Picard functor, no divisor scheme.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_forall_residueField_lift_from_divScheme` — DJ-1's qc
41	  step from per-point lifts.
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` and
43	  `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts` — the two `JacobianData` producers
44	  with the surjectivity hypothesis replaced by per-point lifts.
45	
46	## What this does NOT do
47	
48	It produces no lift.  Producing one is the divRep-gated mathematics of §2.3 (the
49	`fiberTwist` shift plus `exists_effective_of_picClass`, which must stay Challenge-free per
50	§0.5 — `riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`).  What changes is the shape
51	of that obligation: a lift *per point*, stated with no reference to `Function.Surjective`,
52	instead of a global surjectivity claim about a topological map.
53	-/

70	/-- **Per-point residue-field lifts give point surjectivity.**  If every point `y` of `Y`
71	admits a morphism `q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ X` with `q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y`, then the
72	underlying map of `f` is surjective.
73	
74	`Spec κ(y)` is nonempty (a field is nontrivial), and the range of `Y.fromSpecResidueField y`
75	is `{y}` (mathlib `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField`), so the image under `q` of any point
76	of `Spec κ(y)` lies in the fibre of `f` over `y`.

79	quasi-compactness field consumes: `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields a *morphism* out of
80	a residue field, while `quasiCompact_of_surjective` wants a surjection of topological
81	spaces. -/
82	theorem surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift (f : X ⟶ Y)
83	    (h : ∀ y : Y, ∃ q : Spec (Y.residueField y) ⟶ X,
84	      q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y) :
85	    Function.Surjective f.base := by
86	  intro y
87	  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := h y
88	  -- a field is nontrivial, so `Spec κ(y)` has a point
89	  obtain ⟨s⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty (PrimeSpectrum (Y.residueField y)))
90	  refine ⟨q.base s, ?_⟩
91	  have hs : (q ≫ f).base s = (Y.fromSpecResidueField y).base s := by rw [hq]
92	  rw [Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply] at hs
93	  exact hs

95	end Topology
